transcript: The other night, I saw a fantastic new play called Bad Kreyòl by Dominique Morisseau. It's about two cousins Simone and Gigi reconnecting in their homeland of Haiti for the first time in years. Gigi has lived in Haiti her whole life and runs a boutique shop, whereas Simone is visiting from the United States, where she's gone to college and worked corporate. What ensues is a clash of cultural ideas, some jealousy and resentment, and both cousins working through their own questions of personal adequacy and sense of belonging. The themes are universal, but the story and these characters are sculpted in beautiful detail. The writing is rich in specificity and humor, and the story also bakes in headier concepts like colonization, history, capitalism, and exploitation, all without losing sight of the characters and the well-contained plot. The direction is smooth, the acting is great, but the cherry on top is the simple but wonderfully detailed set and costume designs which really elevate the production’s sense of place. Dominique Morisseau has already written a slew of great plays so I knew the writing would be strong, but this piece even exceeded my expectations. I'd consider it a home run. Bad Kreyòl is running at Signature Theater through December 1st and I would definitely recommend. With that, another program for my collection.
